model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of per-specialty medical terms for a base model (Mistralv0.2-Base, shown in light blue) and for the same model fine-tuned on six different medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics (each represented by a distinct shade of orange or brown). The vertical axis, labeled "Negative log probability," ranges from -22 to -27 on a linear scale, with tick marks every 1 unit. The horizontal axis, labeled "Per-specialty terms," displays the six medical specialties in alphabetical order: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics. For each specialty, there are seven bars: the first (light blue) represents the base model's performance, and the next six (in varying shades of orange/brown) represent the performance of the model fine-tuned on each of the six specialties. The chart shows that for each specialty, the fine-tuned model on that specialty achieves the lowest (most negative) negative log probability, indicating better performance. For example, in the "Cardio" group, the base model (light blue) has a negative log probability of approximately -22.2, while the model fine-tuned on Cardio (lightest orange) reaches about -26.2. Similarly, in the "Pediatrics" group, the base model is around -22.5, and the Pediatrics-fine-tuned model (darkest brown) reaches approximately -25.8. The bars are grouped by specialty, with the base model bar consistently appearing first in each group, followed by the fine-tuned models in the order of the legend: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics. The chart visually demonstrates that fine-tuning improves performance on the corresponding specialty, with the most significant improvements observed when the model is fine-tuned on the same specialty as the test terms.
